speeches.speaker: Michael McCormack
speeches.brief: Introduced the ACT Government Loan Bill, which authorises a Commonwealth concessional loan of up to $1 billion to fund the ACT government's loose-fill asbestos remediation program, representing about a fifth of the territory's annual budget, with $750 million appropriated in 2014-15 and the remaining $250 million through the 2015-16 budget.

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: Supported the ACT Government Loan Bill 2014, which would authorise a $1 billion concessional loan for asbestos remediation, including buybacks and demolition of 1,021 affected homes, with $750 million appropriated in this financial year and $250 million in the 2015-16 financial year.

speeches.speaker: David Gillespie
speeches.brief: Supported the ACT Government Loan Bill 2014, which would provide a loan of up to $1 billion for the ACT government to purchase affected properties and address Mr Fluffy asbestos, while warning of the occupational health lessons.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Leigh
speeches.brief: Supported the ACT Government Loan Bill 2014, describing a $750 million concessional loan within a $1 billion facility to buy and demolish 1,021 affected homes, assist families and address the legacy of Mr Fluffy loose-fill asbestos.

speeches.speaker: Nickolas Varvaris
speeches.brief: Supported the ACT Government Loan Bill and its proposed $1 billion concessional loan for an asbestos remediation program involving the purchase and demolition of more than 1,000 affected homes, with $750 million provided in the present financial year and up to $250 million potentially available in the 2015-16 financial year.

speeches.speaker: Keith Pitt
speeches.brief: Supported the ACT Government Loan Bill 2014, describing at length the health dangers of asbestos exposure linked to Mr Fluffy insulation, citing an exposure limit of 0.1 of a fibre per millilitre, and welcomed the Commonwealth's loan of up to $1 billion to help the ACT government demolish affected homes.

speeches.speaker: Peter Hendy
speeches.brief: Supported the ACT Government Loan Bill 2014, explaining the Commonwealth's concessional loan of up to $1 billion to help the ACT government buy back and demolish homes affected by Mr Fluffy loose-fill asbestos, and noted similar cases had been found in the Eden-Monaro electorate.

speeches.speaker: Dennis Jensen
speeches.brief: Supported the ACT Government Loan Bill 2014, noting more than 1,000 houses in the ACT are known to contain Mr Fluffy loose-fill asbestos, welcomed the loan to fund their purchase and demolition, and said the issue helped inform understanding of asbestos risks in the Tangney electorate.

speeches.speaker: Darren Chester
speeches.brief: Supported the ACT Government Loan Bill 2014, praised bipartisan cooperation between the Commonwealth and the ACT government on Mr Fluffy remediation, warned that home renovators face particular asbestos risk, and noted asbestos building products were banned from sale in Australia from December 2003.

speeches.speaker: Michael McCormack
speeches.brief: Reported to the House on the ACT Government Loan Bill 2014, explaining it authorises the Commonwealth to lend the ACT government up to $1 billion for demolition and remediation of Mr Fluffy asbestos-affected homes, appropriated in two stages through the budget process, and thanked members for their contributions to the debate.

speeches.speaker: Laurie Ferguson
speeches.brief: Reported that the Parliamentary Joint Committee on Human Rights had examined 250 bills and 1,717 instruments during 2014, finding 213 bills and 1,707 instruments compatible with human rights, and highlighted the committee's scrutiny of four national security bills as its most challenging work of the year.
